newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr closes softer on U.S. dollar weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr closes softer on U.S. dollar weakness.

text.p: The Canadian dollar ended the day softer on Friday at C$1.3310 (US$0.7514) from Thursday's close at C$1.3290 (US$0.7521) in heavy trading, dealers said.

The Bank of Canada cut short-term interest rates by 25 basis points on Friday morning, after a report that Canada's unemployment rate rose to 10 percent in October from 9.9 percent in September. It was the 11th rate cut this year. The bank has cut rates by 500 basis points since May 1995.
The currency market expected the cut and pushed the Canadian dollar stronger on the news, traders said.
But the currency weakened later in the day after the U.S. dollar lost ground in early trading against other currencies, dealers said.
"My concern right now is the possibility that the U.S. dollar could go a bit lower against the other currencies which could cause some selling of Canada," said one dealer.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dropped to 1.1287 marks from Thursday's close at 1.1378 marks and fell to 83.89 yen from Thursday's 84.31 yen.
